newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-SAMARANCH TO STAND FOR RE-ELECTION.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SAMARANCH TO STAND FOR RE-ELECTION.

text.p: International Olympic Committee (IOC) president Juan Antonio Samaranch announced on Wednesday that he would stand again for re-election to lead the organisation into the 21st century.

Samaranch, who turns 77 in July, said at a news conference that he wanted to be elected for a fourth term in office in a vote to be held in September. If he wins, the Spaniard has the chance to complete 21 years in office after taking over the job in 1980.

Samaranch, who has played a huge role in turning the Olympic movement into a successful commercial outfit in the last two decades, has said for a while that he would carry on if his health was in order.
He is not expected to face opposition in the election by the IOC's members at a session to be held in Lausanne in September.
If he completes his fourth term in office he will be 81 by the time the next election takes place in 2001.
